KEY MESSAGE 1: Dry conditions with gusty winds this afternoon.

Temperatures should peak this afternoon in the low to mid 60s over 
dewpoints in the 30s. RH values this afternoon have already fallen 
into the low to mid 30s, and could fall into the upper 20s 
during the heat of the afternoon. The dry conditions combined 
with gusty west winds could pose a limited fire weather risk for
a few hours this afternoon given continued drought/dry fuels. 
Winds will decrease and RH will recover quickly early this 
evening.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Frost/freeze conditions are possible Friday night 
through Sunday night.

The center of an 1025 mb high will push south over the Mid West 
tonight. As the high builds south, steady H85 CAA is forecast to 
occur until 12Z Saturday, with values between 0 to -2C. Using a 
blend of guidance, low temperatures Saturday morning are forecast to 
range from the mid 30s inland to the low to mid 40s across the 
coastal counties. Northwest winds should range between 5 to 8 mph 
through much of tonight, but could decouple during the pre-dawn 
hours. Given temperatures in the mid 30s, light to calm winds, and 
RH in the 90s, areas to patchy frost is expected along and west of 
the I-95 corridor. The area has been highlighted with a Frost 
Advisory from 2-8 AM Saturday.

Saturday and Saturday Night: High pressure will be spread along the 
mid and upper MS Valley, with it's periphery stretching into the 
Southeast U.S. Northerly winds will continue to usher cold air into 
our area. Thickness values and 850 mb temperatures point towards 
colder temperatures than what some of the MOS has, and we leaned 
this way with the forecast. Despite full sunshine, high temperatures 
may struggle to reach the 60 degree mark, which is about 10 degrees 
below normal for this time of year. The combination of clear skies 
and calm or very light north to northeasterly winds will lead to 
plenty of radiational cooling. Lows should range from the upper 20s 
in the coldest spots far inland to around freezing closer to the 
coast, with coastal counties generally in the mid to upper 30s, and 
the beaches generally in the 40s. Since there is still some 
uncertainty with the temperatures, we maintained the Freeze Watch. 
Plus, this matches our surrounding offices. Though, adjustments may 
be needed with the areal coverage when it's upgraded to a warning. 
Additionally, there will be frost within the current watch and 
closer to the coast (where there are no watches).

Sunday and Sunday Night: High pressure along the mid and upper MS 
Valley in the morning will slowly shift eastward towards the OH 
Valley, with it's periphery continuing to stretch into the Southeast 
U.S. Winds may shift a bit to the northeast during the day, and 
continue to usher cold air into our area. Once again, we leaned 
towards the colder end of guidance. Once again, with plenty of 
sunshine, high temperatures may struggle to reach the 60 degree 
mark. Calm winds and clear skies will lead to plenty of radiational 
cooling the first half of the night. Though, increasing high clouds 
and light winds may limit the full cooling potential the second half 
of the night. As a result, lows should be around freezing very far 
inland, the mid to upper 30s closer to the coast, with locations at 
and near the beaches reaching well into the 40s.

If we have widespread freezing temperatures Saturday night into 
Sunday morning, then that will end our local growing season, and no 
Frost/Freeze products will be needed Sunday night into Monday 
morning. But if only some areas reach freezing, then the growing 
season and Frost/Freeze products will continue Sunday night into 
Monday morning. Either way, temperatures will be colder than
normal.
